extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners before the USPTO (attorneys/agents) and parties/respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, findings, and imposed sanctions in a USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline Final Order resolving neglect and failure-to-notify client matters under the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility. Describes violations, mitigating/remedial actions, required CLE, reporting and notice procedures, and enforcement/remedy mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal basis for OED/USPTO authority to accept settlement agreements, adjudicate, and impose discipline under cited statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner subject to Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner registered to practice before the USPTO is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that registered practitioners (attorneys/agents) must comply with the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility; registration number of respondent cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation — failing to inform a client of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6), via § 10.23(c)(8), by failing to inform a client of correspondence received from the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner receives Notices of Allowance, Fee(s) Due, Office Actions or Notices of Abandonment and does not notify the client; failure to notify can constitute disciplinary misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation — neglecting legal matters entrusted to practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) by neglecting legal matters entrusted to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers failure to timely respond to Office Actions, failure to pay issue fees resulting in abandonment, and failure to revive applications — conduct that constitutes neglect under the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Settlement Agreement must satisfy 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement resolving disciplinary action must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements submitted to the USPTO Director must include stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and meet procedural/regulatory prerequisites under § 11.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution as mitigating/remedial action
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent made restitution to the client for the increased fees and costs incurred with reviving the abandoned applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of restitution to the affected client is a relevant remedial step and mitigating circumstance considered in disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health/medical condition as mitigating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's untreated severe clinical depression contributed to overlooking responsibilities and deadlines; Respondent is receiving medical assistance and treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented medical/psychological condition may be offered as mitigation and can influence the sanctioning decision and required remedial measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial systems implementation (docketing improvements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has purchased and is implementing a new computerized docketing system for patent cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation of improved case management/docketing systems is a remedial measure that addresses causes of neglect and is relevant to sanctioning and probation conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension and stay structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent be suspended from practicing before the Office for twelve (12) months and that all twelve (12) months of the suspension be immediately stayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanction may include a suspension term that is stayed, effectively imposing probationary oversight rather than immediate suspension, depending on compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a 12-month probationary period commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation accompanies stayed suspension and triggers reporting, monitoring, and conditions that must be satisfied during the probationary term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory continuing legal education (CLE) on case management
rubrics_metrics.description: Within six months from the date of the Final Order, enroll, complete, and receive CLE credit under the Rules of the Texas State Bar for at least one course where the primary subject matter is case management (calendaring and communicating with clients) for small firms and/or solo practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within seven months provide corroborating proof of successful completion including: (a) documentary evidence of attendance and completion, (b) description of course content, and (c) copy of written materials provided to participants or other corroborating proof acceptable to the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary reporting obligations — content and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: During probation, submit reports to the OED Director at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months containing detailed disclosures about applications and communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each report shall: (1) identify by application number each U.S. utility patent application entrusted to Respondent in which a Notice of Abandonment was issued during probation predicated on failure to file timely/proper response to any Office communication; (2) state whether, how, and when Respondent reported the Office communication to the client prior to abandonment; (3) provide documentary evidence that Respondent reported the Office communication to the client prior to abandonment (e.g., correspondence copies); (4) state whether, how, and when Respondent reported the Notice of Abandonment to the client; (5) state whether, how, and when Respondent counseled the client about the abandonment, including whether counseling occurred in adequate time to avoid abandonment; (6) provide documentary evidence that Respondent reported the Notice of Abandonment and counseled the client about it (e.g., correspondence copies); and (7) for each application where Respondent did not counsel the client in adequate time to avoid abandonment, identify each application by number and each client by full name and address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary Final Orders are public and publication is an element of discipline and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the specified Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the discipline, the regulatory violations, and summarizing the conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must identify the practitioner, registration number, the violation(s) (citing regs), and a short factual summary; the Order supplies the precise notice text to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the States where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for cross-notification of disciplinary action to external enforcement authorities and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause and immediate suspension procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If during probation the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or violated disciplinary rules or allowed an application to go abandoned without client knowledge, the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent, and grant fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After consideration of any response, if the OED Director remains of that opinion, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director for imposition of an immediate suspension: (i) the Order to Show Cause, (ii) Respondent's response, and (iii) supporting evidence, and request immediate suspension up to twelve (12) months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of suspension does not stay immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director suspends Respondent and Respondent seeks review of that decision, such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the immediate suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review does not automatically stay the imposed immediate suspension; suspension remains effective pending review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance obligations if suspended during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended during any portion of the 12-month probationary period pursuant to the Final Order, Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and obligations for suspended practitioners (e.g., notice to clients, withdrawal, etc.) are governed by § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED duties if suspension imposed during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended during any portion of the 12-month probationary period, the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED must provide appropriate notices to courts, disciplinary authorities and public as required by § 11.59 when a suspension is imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limit on number of suspensions under the Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Proposed Settlement Agreement or the Final Order shall limit the number of times during probation that Respondent may be suspended pursuant to the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order permits multiple suspensions during the probationary period for repeated or continuing violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may seek further discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19–11.57
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order does not prevent the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 through 11.57 for any misconduct engaged in prior to, during, or after his probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement does not constitute a bar to additional enforcement action for separate misconduct; full regulatory range remains available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of record as aggravating factor in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered when addressing any further complaint or evidence of same/similar misconduct and in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past disciplinary findings can be used to aggravate sanctions or counter representations by respondent in later matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party responsible for its own expenses related to the disciplinary proceeding and settlement implementation.
